page: Microsoft Azure D48a_v4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the DAv4 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per core, and includes a bundled 1229 GB local SSD. The hypervisor layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. The Passmark memory score is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10%. However, memory bandwidth for large blocks remains in the middle 50% tier, with read speeds at 104.2 GB/sec and write speeds at 57.59 GB/sec. Large-scale LLM text generation represents a performance bottleneck, with the 70B model achieving only 2.7 tokens/sec, placing it in the bottom 25%.

The instance offers a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and local SSD storage, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high multi-threaded CPU throughput without the premium of memory-optimized hardware classes. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded data decompression, image processing, ray tracing, and general-purpose application hosting. It is less suitable for large-scale LLM inference due to the lack of GPU acceleration and lower text generation throughput on large models.
